note: The Polaris verification conformance cases. Each case names the `artifact` it is about (default `authenticity-pack`), references a published vector, and states the verdict a conformant verifier MUST return; the runner checks every key the case constrains. `anchors: "self"` means the pack's own public key is trusted; `now` pins the evaluation time for a windowed artifact. See SPEC.md and docs/reference/WIRE-SPEC.md. Each case carries `since`, the protocol release that introduced it: a verifier pinned at an older release MUST agree on every case at or before its release and MUST NOT accept anything a later case expects rejected (the cross-version rule, wire spec section 6).

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-stale
cases.note: v9.430: the same genuine artifact, read long after it expired. A verifier that ignores expiry accepts an arbitrarily old answer, which for a revocation feed means a revoked credential keeps verifying.

cases.name: revocation-feed-commitment-mismatch

Its only refusal case tampered the SIGNATURE and left commitment_ok true, so nothing published exercised the commitment at all: a verifier that never recomputed the revoked root conformed, and an authority could sign one root while publishing different leaves.

cases.name: id-token-wrong-audience
cases.note: the SAME valid token, offered to a different relying party. Its signature is perfectly good; accepting it is audience confusion. A verifier that checks only the signature passes every other case in this suite and fails here.

cases.name: id-token-wrong-nonce
cases.note: the right relying party, the wrong login. The nonce binds the token to ONE authentication; without it a token captured from an earlier login is replayable.

cases.name: id-token-expired
cases.note: authentic and expired are different answers. The signature stays good forever; the window does not.

cases.name: id-token-accepted-by-its-own-relying-party
cases.note: the positive control for the three above: without it a verifier that answered False to every question would pass them all.

cases.name: id-token-trusted-issuer

cases.name: pack-mldsa87-valid

cases.name: pack-mldsa87-tampered
cases.note: P8.8a: one flipped signature byte under ML-DSA-87.

cases.name: pack-mldsa44-unaccepted

cases.name: status-assertion-mldsa87-active
cases.note: P8.8a: the status assertion under ML-DSA-87.

cases.name: trust-list-migration
cases.note: P8.8a: an algorithm migration recorded in a trust list: the ML-DSA-65 key retired, the ML-DSA-87 key active and signing.

cases.name: trust-list-migration-retired-signer

cases.name: exchange-receipt-valid
cases.note: P8.2: the responder-signed receipt a service holds after an exchange; evidence without the payload.

cases.name: exchange-receipt-tampered
cases.note: P8.2: the response commitment changed after signing.

cases.name: exchange-mint-valid
cases.note: P8.2b: the statement a responder's service signs to mint a receipt; `algorithm` rides unsigned.

cases.name: exchange-mint-tampered
cases.note: P8.2b: the responder agency changed after signing.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-valid
cases.note: P9.6: the inclusion proof reconstructs a head the expected log key signed.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-witnessed
cases.note: P9.6: two distinct trusted witnesses have cosigned this exact head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-unwitnessed
cases.note: P9.6: anchored, but nobody the verifier trusts has cosigned the head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-forged-head
cases.note: P9.6: a stolen log key can sign a fabricated head; it cannot make a trusted witness cosign it.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-broken-proof
cases.note: P9.6: the path does not reconstruct the head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-forged-cosignature
cases.note: both cosigners are trusted and one of the two signatures is forged, so the threshold of two is not met. Counting a cosignature without verifying it makes the witness quorum arithmetic rather than evidence.

cases.name: trust-attestation-valid
cases.note: P9.5: the attesting agency signed this edge itself; it is not the operator's word.

cases.name: trust-attestation-rekeyed
cases.note: P9.5: the edge is bound to the attested KEY, so re-pointing it at another key breaks it.

cases.name: trust-attestation-widened
cases.note: P9.5: the context is signed, so an edge cannot be widened after the fact.

cases.name: trust-attestation-from-another-agency
cases.note: the SAME valid attestation, offered as though agency 3 had signed it. The signature is good; it is simply not from the agency the relying party is asking about. A verifier that checks only the signature accepts it.

cases.name: trust-attestation-for-another-key
cases.note: the attestation is genuine and it attests a DIFFERENT key than the one being relied on. The edge has to bind to the key actually in hand.

cases.name: trust-attestation-accepted-for-its-own-agency-and-key
cases.note: the positive control for the two above: without it a verifier that refused every attestation would pass them both.

cases.name: holder-binding-valid
cases.note: P9.1: the issuer's signed statement that this holder key belongs to this credential.

cases.name: holder-binding-tampered
cases.note: P9.1: the bound key was swapped after signing.

cases.name: holder-binding-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: holder-binding-stale
cases.note: v9.430: the same genuine artifact, read long after it expired. A verifier that ignores expiry accepts an arbitrarily old answer, which for a revocation feed means a revoked credential keeps verifying.

cases.name: holder-binding-trusted-issuer
cases.note: v9.431: the same genuine artifact, read by a relying party who trusts the key that signed it.

cases.name: holder-binding-untrusted-issuer

cases.name: holder-proof-valid
cases.note: P9.1: the holder's own signature over the credential, context, nonce and instant.

cases.name: holder-proof-tampered
cases.note: v9.429: holder-proof had one case and it expected authentic: true. The holder-chain refusals each fail for a non-signature reason (a stranger's key, a replayed nonce, a revoked binding), so forcing the signature check permissive left every case green.

cases.name: holder-proof-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: holder-proof-stale
cases.note: v9.430: the same genuine artifact, read long after it expired. A verifier that ignores expiry accepts an arbitrarily old answer, which for a revocation feed means a revoked credential keeps verifying.

cases.name: holder-chain-proved
cases.note: P9.1: the party presenting the credential holds the key its issuer bound to it.

cases.name: holder-chain-stranger
cases.note: P9.1: a genuine proof by a key the issuer never bound proves nothing about this credential.

cases.name: holder-chain-replayed
cases.note: P9.1: a proof naming another verifier's nonce is a replay of one made for somebody else.

cases.name: holder-chain-revoked
cases.note: P9.1: a revoked binding means the holder has no usable key until a new one is bound.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-valid
cases.note: P9.2: the published anonymity set, signed, with the leaves committed by leaves_root_hex.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-swapped
cases.note: P9.2: a member swapped after signing; the commitment no longer matches the set.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-stale

cases.name: epoch-leaves-trusted-issuer
cases.note: v9.431: the same genuine artifact, read by a relying party who trusts the key that signed it.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-untrusted-issuer

cases.name: agent-grant-valid
cases.note: P9.8: a holder-signed grant naming its actions, limits and expiry.

cases.name: agent-grant-widened
cases.note: P9.8: an action was added after signing. actions is inside the signed statement precisely so this fails.

cases.name: agent-grant-fresh
cases.note: v9.430: `now` is pinned so freshness is testable forever. Without a pinned instant the answer drifts with the calendar, which is why the contract never asserted it: five of the published vectors had already expired and no case noticed, because none asked.

cases.name: agent-grant-stale
cases.note: v9.430: the same genuine artifact, read long after it expired. A verifier that ignores expiry accepts an arbitrarily old answer, which for a revocation feed means a revoked credential keeps verifying.

cases.name: grant-revocation-valid
cases.note: P9.8: the holder ends the grant with the same key that signed it. The issuer is not contacted and the human's credential is untouched.

cases.name: grant-revocation-impostor
cases.note: P9.8: the SIGNATURE is genuine, but by a key that is not the grant's holder. A verifier must check that binding separately: authenticity alone does not end a grant, or anyone able to publish bytes could revoke somebody else's.

cases.name: grant-revocation-tampered
cases.note: v9.429: as for agent-proof. A revocation whose signature nobody verifies is a revocation anyone can mint, which ends a grant that is still valid.

cases.name: agent-proof-valid
cases.note: P9.8: the agent's signature over the grant, the action and the service's nonce.

cases.name: agent-proof-impostor
cases.note: P9.8: genuinely signed, by a key the grant does not name. Without the key-matches-grant check a copied grant would be a bearer token.

cases.name: agent-proof-tampered
cases.note: v9.429: every published agent-proof case expected authentic: true, including the impostor one (a genuine signature by the wrong key is authentic and powerless). So no case exercised the signature at all, and a verifier that never checked it conformed.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-widened-grant
cases.note: An action added to the grant after signing. A grant the holder did not sign grants nothing, so its scope is not read at all: answering from the forged list would honour the forger's own action.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-in-scope
cases.note: The requested action is in the grant's signed scope.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-out-of-scope
cases.note: A genuine grant used for an action it does not name. Authenticity is not permission.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-revoked-by-holder
cases.note: The holder's own revocation of this grant ends it.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-revocation-by-impostor
cases.note: A genuinely signed revocation by a key that is not the grant's holder ends nothing; otherwise anyone able to publish bytes could revoke somebody else's grant.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-agent-proved
cases.note: The agent proves it holds the key the grant names, for this action and this nonce.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-proof-by-impostor
cases.note: A genuine proof by a key the grant does not name: a copied grant is not a bearer token.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-proof-replayed
cases.note: The agent's genuine proof, presented to a service that issued a different nonce: a replay.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-bound
cases.note: The grant is signed by the key the credential's issuer bound to the holder, under an active binding. The verifier's handle for this principal is pairwise, and still a stable value it can store: correlation is exposed, not bounded.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-binding-revoked
cases.note: The issuer revoked the holder's binding (a lost device). A grant signed with that key speaks for nobody: a revoked binding means the holder has no usable key.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-stranger
cases.note: A genuine grant signed by a key no issuer bound to this credential.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-binding-wrong-type
cases.note: A genuinely issuer-signed object of ANOTHER type, carrying a binding's fields outside what that type signs. Only its format says it is not a binding.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-authorized
cases.note: The envelope is by the requester expected, attested in its context by a trusted authority whose manifest is fresh at `now`, and the body held is the one it commits to.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-other-requester
cases.note: A genuine envelope from a requester other than the one this party expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-context-not-attested
cases.note: The requester is attested in context 1, and this envelope is for context 3. Trust is in-context.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-forged-manifest
cases.note: The only attestation for context 3 was added to the manifest after the authority signed it, so the authority never said it.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-attestation-expired
cases.note: The requester's attestation in context 2 closed an hour before `now`; the manifest carrying it is still fresh, and the attestation's own window decides.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-manifest-stale
cases.note: The same envelope and manifest, decided at an instant after the manifest expired. The decision is made at the stated `now`, not at whatever the verifier's clock says.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-other-body
cases.note: A body other than the one the envelope's request_hash commits to.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-stranger-signed
cases.note: A genuine signature by a stranger's key over an envelope naming the requester: the key that verifies must be the requester the signed statement claims. An envelope that is not the requester's answers nothing further.

cases.name: exchange-use-request-tampered
cases.note: The context changed after signing. A forged envelope answers nothing further.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-authorized
cases.note: The receipt is by the responder expected; a trusted authority attests the requester in the receipt's context (`via` names it); both bodies, as exchanged, match the commitments; and it names the responder it was signed by.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-other-responder
cases.note: A genuine receipt from a responder other than the one this party expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-context-not-attested
cases.note: The requester is attested in context 1, and this receipt is for context 3.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-no-context
cases.note: A genuinely signed receipt that states no context, beside a fresh trusted manifest attesting the requester in context 1. Attested in the receipt's context means that context exactly: before 1.0.0-rc.64 the detached verifier accepted an attestation from ANY context here.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-nameless-authority
cases.note: A genuine, fresh manifest attests the requester in the receipt's context but names no authority. A receipt's authorization answers BY WHOM (`via`), and a manifest that names nobody cannot be that answer.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-manifest-stale
cases.note: The same receipt and manifest, decided after the manifest expired.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-other-bodies
cases.note: Bodies other than the ones the receipt commits to.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-body-reserialized
cases.note: The same request re-serialized with whitespace. A receipt commits to the body bytes as exchanged, so a verifier hashes the body as given and does not re-serialize it.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-tampered
cases.note: The context changed after signing. A forged receipt answers nothing further, and names no responder: its `responder` field is the forger's word.

cases.name: exchange-use-mint-responder-matches
cases.note: The mint statement is signed by the responder expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-mint-other-responder
cases.note: A genuine mint statement by a key other than the responder this party expected.

cases.name: exchange-use-mint-tampered
cases.note: The context changed after signing; a forged mint answers nothing further.

cases.name: transplant-manifest-genuine
cases.note: The artifact whose signature the next case moves: a genuine manifest by the transplant authority.

cases.name: pack-transplanted-artifact-signature
cases.note: The manifest's genuine signature and canonical statement, wrapped as a pack, with its key trusted. A pack's token_value MUST be a credential serial (WIRE-SPEC 3.7): every other artifact signs a JSON statement, which begins with '{'. Before 1.0.0-rc.64 every shipped verifier reported this authentic and its issuer trusted.

cases.name: pack-transplant-control-valid
cases.note: Control: the same authority's key over a credential serial verifies and is trusted, so the refusal above is the serial rule's and not the key's.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-signed-open
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: the edge is signed and its own window is open at now: the positive control.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-signed-closed
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: the edge is signed and its own window closed a month before now; the manifest is fresh.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-unsigned-open
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: a legacy edge states a window that is open at now: the positive control.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-window-unsigned-closed
cases.note: Wire spec section 4: a legacy edge states a window that closed before now: the manifest's authority signed that window, and a fresh manifest does not extend an edge its authority has ended.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-base
cases.note: The positive control: the genuine setup every variant below differs from in one fact.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-clean
cases.note: The positive control for the feed variants: an authentic, fresh feed from the issuer that revokes nothing.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-manifest-stale
cases.note: A manifest past its own window confers nothing, however genuine.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-attestation-other-key
cases.note: An edge that attests another key does not attest this credential's issuer.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-attestation-bad-signature
cases.note: A present-but-invalid edge signature refuses the edge (wire spec section 3.14).

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-retired-anchor
cases.note: Trusting only a key the manifest lists as RETIRED confers no trust in it.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-stale
cases.note: A supplied feed must be fresh (wire spec section 4, item 3): fail-closed.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-other-issuer
cases.note: A supplied feed must be bound to the issuer's key: another authority's word about this credential is not the issuer's.

cases.name: cross-authority-variants-feed-not-authentic
cases.note: A supplied feed must be authentic: a forged or altered one rejects.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-variants-base
cases.note: The positive control: this log's genuine head, the inclusion proof, and two distinct trusted witnesses cosigning exactly that head.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-variants-other-log
cases.note: A head genuinely signed by the log's key but for ANOTHER log does not anchor an entry of this one.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-variants-cosignature-other-size
cases.note: The second cosignature is genuine but over another tree size, so it is not a cosignature of this head and the threshold of two is not met.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-variants-cosignature-other-root
cases.note: The second cosignature is genuine but over another root, so it witnesses a different log state and the threshold of two is not met.

cases.name: holder-chain-proof-window-late-edge
cases.note: The binding is valid throughout, so only the proof's own window decides: five minutes after the proof: the last instant it is fresh.

cases.name: holder-chain-proof-window-late-past
cases.note: The binding is valid throughout, so only the proof's own window decides: one second past the five-minute window.

cases.name: holder-chain-proof-window-early-edge
cases.note: The binding is valid throughout, so only the proof's own window decides: one minute before the proof: the clock skew allowed.

cases.name: holder-chain-proof-window-early-past
cases.note: The binding is valid throughout, so only the proof's own window decides: one second more skew than is allowed.

cases.name: cross-authority-uppercase-leaf-no-feed
cases.note: The positive control: the same credential, with no feed supplied, is accepted.

cases.name: cross-authority-uppercase-leaf-revoked
cases.note: The issuer's authentic feed lists the leaf in upper-case hex. Leaves are hex and compared without regard to case, as the feed's own commitment is.

cases.name: cross-authority-require-signed-unsigned-edge
cases.note: The relying party requires signed edges and this one is legacy (wire spec 3.14).

cases.name: cross-authority-require-signed-signed-edge
cases.note: The positive control: under the same requirement a signed edge is accepted.

cases.name: cross-authority-unsigned-edge-not-required
cases.note: The same legacy edge with the option off is accepted: the option decides.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-cosignatures-not-a-list
cases.note: The genuine anchor with its cosignatures replaced by true: anchored, and no witness. Two verifiers raised.

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-format-not-a-string
cases.note: A genuine checkpoint whose format is a list: an unknown artifact, not an exception.

cases.name: cross-authority-feed-not-an-object
cases.note: A revocation feed that is not an object cannot establish non-revocation: reject, not an exception.

cases.name: pack-signature-hex-not-hex
cases.note: A hex field holds hex digits and nothing else: a byte of signature_hex written with a character that is not hex; a reader that stops at the first bad character decodes the genuine signature. Before this case the TypeScript SDK accepted a character that is not hex and the Python verifiers accepted whitespace, each where the others refused.

cases.name: pack-signature-hex-whitespace
cases.note: A hex field holds hex digits and nothing else: a space between two bytes of signature_hex; a reader that skips whitespace decodes the genuine signature. Before this case the TypeScript SDK accepted a character that is not hex and the Python verifiers accepted whitespace, each where the others refused.

cases.name: pack-public-key-hex-not-hex
cases.note: A hex field holds hex digits and nothing else: a byte of public_key_hex written with a character that is not hex; a reader that stops at the first bad character decodes the genuine key. Before this case the TypeScript SDK accepted a character that is not hex and the Python verifiers accepted whitespace, each where the others refused.

cases.name: federation-status-bundle-count-mismatch
cases.note: WIRE-SPEC 3.4: member_count MUST equal the number of members. The root matches the one member listed and the signed count says two; before this case both SDKs accepted it and only the detached verifier refused.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-proof-index-not-a-number
cases.note: An inclusion proof's index and tree size are JSON integers and its path a list (WIRE-SPEC, anchoring): an index of false, which int() and Number() both read as 0. Read leniently it is the genuine one-leaf proof of timestamp-anchor-variants-base; before this case the three verifiers each accepted it.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-proof-size-not-a-number
cases.note: An inclusion proof's index and tree size are JSON integers and its path a list (WIRE-SPEC, anchoring): a tree size written as the string "1", which int() and Number() both read as 1. Read leniently it is the genuine one-leaf proof of timestamp-anchor-variants-base; before this case the three verifiers each accepted it.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-proof-path-not-a-list
cases.note: An inclusion proof's index and tree size are JSON integers and its path a list (WIRE-SPEC, anchoring): an audit path that is an object, which `or []` and a non-array fallback both read as the empty path. Read leniently it is the genuine one-leaf proof of timestamp-anchor-variants-base; before this case the three verifiers each accepted it.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-credential-forged
cases.note: WIRE-SPEC 3.17 names the issuer's signature on the credential as a link a verifier MUST check. The binding names this credential and is signed by its key, and the credential's signature does not verify; before this case all three verifiers bound the grant to it.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-no-credential
cases.note: A binding with no credential beside it binds the holder key to nothing a verifier has checked; before this case the detached verifier bound it.

cases.name: holder-chain-proof-for-another-credential
cases.note: The holder's genuine signature over a proof naming ANOTHER credential, presented with this one. `token_value` is inside what the holder signs (WIRE-SPEC 3.15), so the proof is about the other credential. Before this case every verifier here compared only the proof's key with the binding's.

cases.name: holder-chain-proof-for-this-credential
cases.note: The positive control: the same chain and holder key, with the proof naming this credential.

cases.name: cross-authority-manifest-lists-trusted-anchor
cases.note: The manifest is signed by the attacker's root and LISTS the published anchor, whose private key signed nothing here, beside it. WIRE-SPEC section 4: a manifest the relying party trusts is "signed by a trusted anchor". Before this case all three verifiers here trusted a manifest when any key it listed was trusted, and accepted the attacker's credential.

cases.name: cross-authority-manifest-signer-trusted
cases.note: The positive control: the same pack and manifest, with the relying party trusting the key that signed the manifest. The refusal in cross-authority-manifest-lists-trusted-anchor is the trust rule's, not a broken vector's.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-signed-by-a-stranger
cases.note: A trusted authority's manifest whose one edge carries a valid signature by a key that is none of the authority's anchors, with a signed edge required. WIRE-SPEC 3.14: an edge is "signed by the agency that made it". Before this case every verifier here counted any key's signature.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-signed-by-its-authority
cases.note: The positive control: the same edge signed by the authority's own root, with a signed edge required.

cases.name: timestamp-rules-control
cases.note: The positive control for the timestamp-rule cases: the same key, a lowercase SHA3-256 digest.

cases.name: timestamp-digest-algorithm-not-sha3
cases.note: WIRE-SPEC 3.9: digest_algorithm MUST be SHA3-256. Signed and otherwise well formed; before this case all three verifiers here accepted it.

cases.name: timestamp-digest-hex-uppercase
cases.note: WIRE-SPEC 3.9: digest_hex MUST be the LOWERCASE SHA3-256 hex. Before this case all three verifiers here accepted the uppercase spelling.

cases.name: timestamp-issued-at-not-an-instant
cases.note: A timestamp binds a digest to an instant, and 31 February is none. Before this case both SDKs accepted it; the detached verifier refused it.

cases.name: revocation-feed-rules-control
cases.note: The positive control for the feed-count cases: two leaves, counted as two.

cases.name: revocation-feed-count-mismatch
cases.note: WIRE-SPEC 3.3: revoked_count MUST equal the number of distinct leaves. The root matches the two leaves and the signed count says one; before this case both SDKs accepted it.

cases.name: revocation-feed-count-not-a-number
cases.note: A count of true is not one leaf (WIRE-SPEC section 1): before this case the detached verifier read it as 1.

cases.name: federation-manifest-rules-control
cases.note: The positive control: the manifest is signed by its own declared active anchor.

cases.name: federation-manifest-signed-by-a-stranger
cases.note: WIRE-SPEC 3.1: a manifest MUST be signed by one of its own active anchors, so a stranger key cannot mint one. Every verifier here enforced it and nothing pinned it: with the rule removed from all three, every suite still passed.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-head-is-an-sth
cases.note: The positive control: a one-leaf log, its signed tree head by the log key, and the inclusion proof of this timestamp in it.

cases.name: timestamp-anchor-head-is-not-an-sth
cases.note: The same proof under a head that is a genuine timestamp the log key signed, with the tree fields attached outside what a timestamp signs. Signed by the log key is not a head of the log; before this case both SDKs here anchored it.

cases.name: holder-chain-no-nonce
cases.note: The genuine chain of holder-chain-proof-for-this-credential, checked against no verifier nonce. A proof checked against no challenge is replayable (WIRE-SPEC 3.15: MUST require verifier_nonce to equal the one it issued); before this case both SDKs here proved it.

cases.name: holder-chain-credential-signature-forged
cases.note: The same chain and nonce, with one byte of the credential's own signature flipped. A binding to a credential that does not verify binds a key to nothing; before this case both SDKs here proved it.

cases.name: holder-chain-binding-current
cases.note: The positive control: a fresh proof under a binding inside its window.

cases.name: holder-chain-binding-expired
cases.note: The same chain, issuer and proof under a binding whose window closed a month earlier: the issuer vouches for the holder key only inside it. Both SDKs refused it; the detached verifier's contract adapter never read the binding's window.

cases.name: exchange-use-receipt-responder-unconfirmed
cases.note: The receipt of exchange-use-receipt-authorized, checked with no responder key. It names its responder in the statement its signer wrote, so the name is a claim until the key is confirmed; before this case every verifier here reported it.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-grant-fresh
cases.note: The positive control: the grant of agent-grant-use-action-in-scope, inside its window.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-grant-expired
cases.note: The same grant thirty seconds after its expires_at. WIRE-SPEC 2.2: a verifier MUST reject an artifact outside its window. Before this case the contract asked only whether the grant was genuine, and an expired grant came back in scope.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-binding-windowed
cases.note: The positive control: the issuer bound the holder's key under a binding with a window, and the grant is signed by that key.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-binding-without-window
cases.note: The same chain and issuer key with the binding's window left out, which WIRE-SPEC 2.2 makes unacceptable. Before this case both SDKs here read it as fresh; the detached verifier refused it.

cases.name: manifest-signer-status-active
cases.note: The positive control: a manifest signed by its one anchor, listed active.

cases.name: manifest-signer-status-empty
cases.note: The same manifest with its signer's anchor entry signed as ''. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed '' as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: manifest-signer-status-false
cases.note: The same manifest with its signer's anchor entry signed as False. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed False as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: registry-publisher-status-active
cases.note: The positive control: the published registry re-signed by a fresh publisher key it lists as active.

cases.name: registry-publisher-status-empty
cases.note: The same registry with its publisher's entry signed as ''. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed '' as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: holder-chain-binding-status-active
cases.note: The positive control: an active binding inside its window.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-binding-status-active
cases.note: The positive control: an active binding inside its window.

cases.name: holder-chain-binding-status-empty
cases.note: The same chain under a binding the issuer signed with status ''. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed '' as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-binding-status-empty
cases.note: The same grant under a binding the issuer signed with status ''. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed '' as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: holder-chain-binding-status-false
cases.note: The same chain under a binding the issuer signed with status False. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed False as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-binding-status-false
cases.note: The same grant under a binding the issuer signed with status False. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed False as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-anchor-status-active
cases.note: The positive control: the edge is signed by an anchor its authority lists as active, with a signed edge required.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-anchor-status-empty
cases.note: The same edge, its signer listed by the authority with status '', with a signed edge required. A status that is absent means active; any other value has to BE "active". Before this case the Python SDK and the detached verifier read a signed '' as active and the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: revocation-feed-leaf-rules-control
cases.note: The positive control: the same feed, re-signed, listing one genuine leaf.

cases.name: revocation-feed-leaf-null-python-root
cases.note: A null leaf, its root computed as Python spells it ("none"). Both Python verifiers accepted this feed and the TypeScript SDK refused it.

cases.name: revocation-feed-leaf-null-javascript-root
cases.note: The same null leaf, its root computed as JavaScript spells it ("null"). The TypeScript SDK accepted this feed and both Python verifiers refused it.

cases.name: revocation-feed-leaf-a-number
cases.note: A leaf that is the number 1.0, rooted as Python spells it. A leaf is a SHA3-256, so 64 hex digits; anything else is refused before the root is computed.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-leaf-not-hex
cases.note: A published anonymity set with one entry that is not a SHA3-256, its commitment recomputed over it. Every verifier here accepted it; the entries are SHA3-256 hexes (WIRE-SPEC 3.16), so the set is refused.

cases.name: epoch-leaves-leaf-rules-control
cases.note: The positive control: the published set, re-signed.

cases.name: signed-document-digest-rules-control
cases.note: The positive control: the published document, re-signed.

cases.name: signed-document-digest-algorithm-not-sha3
cases.note: The same document labelled MD5. WIRE-SPEC 3.12: digest_algorithm MUST be SHA3-256. No verifier here checked it.

cases.name: signed-document-digest-hex-uppercase
cases.note: The same digest in upper case. WIRE-SPEC 3.12: digest_hex MUST be lowercase. No verifier here checked it, and the detached verifier's binding compared a lowercased copy.

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-issued-microseconds-ahead
cases.note: A checkpoint issued 100 microseconds after `now`. WIRE-SPEC 2.2: issued_at <= now. The TypeScript SDK rounded both instants to the millisecond and read it as fresh; both Python verifiers read it as not yet valid.

cases.name: epoch-checkpoint-issued-microseconds-behind
cases.note: The positive control: the same checkpoint 100 microseconds after it was issued.

cases.name: timestamp-issued-at-year-0099
cases.note: Year 99, a valid RFC 3339 year. Both Python verifiers read it; the TypeScript SDK's Date.UTC read it as 1999 and its own check then refused the date.

cases.name: timestamp-issued-at-offset-24-hours
cases.note: An offset of 24 hours is not one RFC 3339 allows; the TypeScript SDK read it.

cases.name: timestamp-issued-at-non-ascii-digits
cases.note: A year in Arabic-Indic digits. Python's `\d` matched them and int() converted them.

cases.name: timestamp-issued-at-byte-order-mark
cases.note: A leading byte-order mark, which the TypeScript SDK's trim() removed.

cases.name: timestamp-issued-at-file-separator
cases.note: A leading file separator, which Python's strip() removed.

cases.name: agent-grant-small-amount-limit
cases.note: A genuine grant whose signed max_amount is 0.000015, which the signer writes as 1.5e-05. The TypeScript SDK wrote it as 0.000015 when it rebuilt the statement, and refused the grant.

cases.name: registry-keys-outside-the-bmp
cases.note: A genuine registry whose signed instance holds a key outside the Basic Multilingual Plane. Python sorts it after "\uffff" (code point); the TypeScript SDK sorted it before (UTF-16 unit) and refused the registry.

cases.name: registry-publisher-agency-id-missing
cases.note: A registry whose publisher names no agency id, signed by a key listed for an authority whose id is null. Python's == matched the two; the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: trust-list-publisher-agency-id-true
cases.note: A trust list whose publisher's agency id is the boolean true, signed by a key listed for agency 1. Python's == read True as 1; the TypeScript SDK did not.

cases.name: trust-list-publisher-agency-id-control
cases.note: The positive control: the published trust list, signed by a key it lists for its own publisher.

cases.name: holder-chain-verifier-nonce-control
cases.note: The positive control: a proof naming the relying party's nonce, as text, in context 1.

cases.name: holder-chain-verifier-nonce-boolean
cases.note: A proof whose signed verifier_nonce is the boolean true, checked against the nonce "true". A nonce is text; true is not. The TypeScript SDK's String() spelled it "true" and proved the chain; Python's str() spelled it "True" and did not.

cases.name: holder-chain-verifier-nonce-small-number
cases.note: A proof whose signed verifier_nonce is the number 0.00001 (signed as 1e-05), checked against the nonce "0.00001". The TypeScript SDK's String() wrote "0.00001" and proved the chain; Python's str() wrote "1e-05" and did not.

cases.name: holder-chain-context-boolean
cases.note: A proof whose signed context_id is the boolean true, checked in context 1. Python's == read true as 1 and proved the chain; the TypeScript SDK's === did not. A context is an id, and true is not one.

cases.name: trust-attestation-attesting-agency-control
cases.note: The positive control: an attestation by agency 1, checked for agency 1.

cases.name: trust-attestation-attesting-agency-boolean
cases.note: An attestation whose signed attesting_agency_id is the boolean true, checked for agency 1. Python's == read true as 1 and relied on it; the TypeScript SDK's === did not.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-context-control
cases.note: The positive control: a signed edge in context 1, presented in context 1.

cases.name: cross-authority-edge-context-boolean
cases.note: The same edge signed with context_id true, presented in context 1. Python's == read true as 1 and accepted it; the TypeScript SDK's === did not.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-proof-nonce-control
cases.note: The positive control: a proof naming the grant and the service's nonce, as text.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-proof-names-no-nonce
cases.note: A proof that names no service nonce, checked against an expected nonce of true, which has no wire text. Neither side names a nonce, so nothing matches. The first parity fix compared the two readings bare (None == None, null === null) and proved it in all three verifiers; the published packages refuse it.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-grant-id-beyond-safe-integer
cases.note: A proof whose signed grant_id is the integer 2**53 + 1, for a grant whose id is that number written as text. Python read the exact integer and matched it; JavaScript reads the nearest double, 2**53. An id beyond 2**53 is not one both languages can read.

cases.name: agent-grant-names-itself-control
cases.note: The positive control: a grant whose grant_id, its revocation handle, is text.

cases.name: agent-grant-without-grant-id
cases.note: A grant signed with grant_id null. WIRE-SPEC 3.17: grant_id is the revocation handle and names this grant alone; a grant without one could never be revoked, so it is not a grant. Every verifier here read it as authentic.

cases.name: agent-grant-grant-id-boolean
cases.note: A grant signed with grant_id true, which is not text, so it names no grant and no revocation can name it. Every verifier here read it as authentic.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-revocation-names-grant-control
cases.note: The positive control: the holder revokes the grant named "True", by that text.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-revocation-grant-id-boolean
cases.note: A revocation naming the boolean true, for the grant named "True". Python's str() spelled true "True" and revoked it; the TypeScript SDK's String() spelled it "true" and did not. true is not text, so it names no grant.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-nested-list
cases.note: A grant whose signed actions list holds the list ["read:status"]. The TypeScript SDK's String() read it as "read:status" and found the action in scope; Python's str() did not. An action is text, and a list is not.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-boolean
cases.note: A grant whose signed actions list holds the boolean true, asked for the action "true". The TypeScript SDK's String() spelled it "true" and found it in scope; Python's str() spelled it "True".

cases.name: agent-grant-use-action-null
cases.note: A grant whose signed actions list holds null, asked for the action "None". Python's str() spelled null "None" and found it in scope; the TypeScript SDK's String() spelled it "null".

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-token-text-control
cases.note: The positive control: the issuer binds the grant's signing key to this credential, by its token value.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-token-boolean-javascript
cases.note: A binding the issuer signed with token_value true, beside the credential "true". The TypeScript SDK's String() spelled it "true" and bound the grant; Python did not.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-principal-token-boolean-python
cases.note: The same binding beside the credential "True". Python's str() spelled true "True" and bound the grant; the TypeScript SDK did not. true is not text and names no credential.

cases.name: manifest-anchor-key-control
cases.note: The positive control: a manifest signed by the one anchor it lists.

cases.name: manifest-anchor-key-a-list
cases.note: A manifest signed by K whose one anchor lists its key as [K]. A key or a digest is a hex string; JavaScript's String() read the one-element list as its element, so the TypeScript SDK accepted this and both Python verifiers did not.

cases.name: agent-grant-use-agent-key-a-list
cases.note: A grant naming its agent key as [AK], and a proof signed by AK. A key or a digest is a hex string; JavaScript's String() read the one-element list as its element, so the TypeScript SDK accepted this and both Python verifiers did not.

cases.name: holder-chain-binding-key-a-list
cases.note: A binding the issuer signed naming the holder key as [HK], and a proof signed by HK. A key or a digest is a hex string; JavaScript's String() read the one-element list as its element, so the TypeScript SDK accepted this and both Python verifiers did not.

cases.name: cross-authority-attested-key-a-list
cases.note: A signed edge naming the attested key as [K], presented by a credential signed by K. A key or a digest is a hex string; JavaScript's String() read the one-element list as its element, so the TypeScript SDK accepted this and both Python verifiers did not.

cases.name: revocation-feed-root-a-list
cases.note: A feed whose signed revoked_root_hex is [R], R being the root of its one leaf. A key or a digest is a hex string; JavaScript's String() read the one-element list as its element, so the TypeScript SDK accepted this and both Python verifiers did not.
